items.title: Physical Intelligence Reportedly Seeks $1B at a $20B Valuation
items.summary: Physical Intelligence is reportedly seeking at least $1 billion in funding for a valuation of approximately $20 billion. The company is opening its models to external developers via an API beta to facilitate robot model training and inference. Existing investors Avenir and Lux Capital are in discussions to lead this potential financing round. The company's ambition is to create a shared intelligence layer that can learn across different robot bodies and applications. This development aims to make their research accessible for building real-world applications.
items.audio_script: From Humanoids Daily, Physical Intelligence Reportedly Seeks $1B at a $20B Valuation. This report details the company's current fundraising goal and valuation. Existing investors Avenir and Lux Capital are reportedly in discussions to lead this potential financing round. The company's objective is to establish a shared intelligence layer capable of learning across diverse robot bodies and applications, aiming to make research accessible for real-world application development. This development signals a push toward unified, multi-body artificial intelligence systems. The industry should monitor the progress of this financing and the subsequent development of the shared intelligence framework.

items.title: North American robot orders climb 24.8% in Q3 of 2026, says A3
items.summary: North American robot orders grew 24.8% in units and 26.1% in value in the third quarter of 2026. This growth was driven by positive returns in automotive OEM orders and significant increases across other sectors like semiconductors, life sciences, and plastics. Collaborative robots saw a substantial 56% increase in units during the same period. This positive momentum occurred despite earlier declines in the first half of 2026 for some segments. Overall, the market shows increasing diversification across various industries.
items.audio_script: From The Robot Report, North American robot orders climb 24.8% in Q3 of 2026, says A3. This report details the growth trajectory of robot orders across North America during the third quarter of 2026, revealing a significant increase in both unit volume and monetary value. The growth was fueled by positive returns observed in automotive original equipment manufacturer orders alongside substantial increases in demand across diverse sectors including semiconductors, life sciences, and plastics. Collaborative robots specifically experienced a notable fifty-six percent increase in unit volume during this same period. This positive market momentum occurred despite earlier decreases noted in the first half of 2026 for certain market segments. This trend indicates an increasing diversification of robot adoption across various industrial applications. The data suggests continued broad-based expansion within the advanced manufacturing and technology sectors.

items.title: Maxinsights raises $30 million to build training data platform for physical AI
items.summary: Maxinsights raised $30 million to expand its physical AI data platform, which pays contractors to record real-world activities for robot and AI training data. The company has collected over 2 million hours of human activity, with 1.5 million hours being model-ready, ensuring exposure to real-world variations. They developed MaxLoop for footage quality monitoring and MaxGlove for capturing tactile information like grip force. This data is crucial for training models like Genesis AI, which has used Maxinsights data for its GENE-26.5 model. Maxinsights emphasizes that capturing real-world data, including edge cases, is essential for deploying robots effectively.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, Maxinsights raises thirty million dollars to build a training data platform for physical artificial intelligence, expanding its system for generating real-world activity data for robot and AI training. The company has successfully collected over two million hours of human activity, with one point five million of those hours being made ready for model training, ensuring exposure to real-world variations. To achieve this, Maxinsights developed tools such as MaxLoop for monitoring footage quality and MaxGlove for capturing tactile information like grip force. This collected data is critical for training models such as Genesis AI, which utilized this information for its GENE-26.5 model, underscoring the necessity of capturing real-world data, including edge cases, for effective robot deployment. This development indicates a growing industry focus on high-fidelity physical data collection for advancing autonomous systems.

items.title: Pairing industrial AI autonomy and human control
items.source: MIT Technology Review - AI & Emerging Tech
items.summary: Living digital twins combine high-fidelity operational data with control systems to mirror industrial plant dynamism. AI is central to evolving these twins into adaptive, living models that can intervene in the physical world. Agentic AI enables systems to act autonomously in select areas, balancing human oversight to define acceptable operational boundaries. This requires robust data synchronization through technologies like IoT sensors and predictive models to create a connected operational record. Ultimately, this integration across the value chain promises greater resilience and sustainable industrial operation.
items.audio_script: From MIT Technology Review - AI & Emerging Tech, "Pairing industrial AI autonomy and human control". This story explores the integration of industrial artificial intelligence with human control mechanisms to achieve adaptive operational models. Living digital twins combine high-fidelity operational data with control systems to mirror industrial plant dynamism, and artificial intelligence is central to evolving these twins into adaptive, living models capable of intervening in the physical world. Agentic AI facilitates systems acting autonomously within defined parameters, requiring robust data synchronization from IoT sensors and predictive models to maintain a connected operational record. This integration across the value chain is projected to yield increased resilience and sustainable industrial operation. items.title: A soft robot could help doctors diagnose and treat disorders of the small intestine
items.summary: MIT engineers developed a robotic enteroscope inspired by snakes to navigate the small intestine for easier diagnosis and treatment. This soft robot uses multifunctional actuators and textured coatings to move through narrow passages by mimicking snake locomotion. It is equipped with tools for imaging, drug delivery, and taking biopsies of polyps. The system allows external controllers to guide the robot through the intestine. Animal studies demonstrated the robot's capability to travel several feet while performing these interventions.
items.audio_script: From MIT News - Robotics, "A soft robot could help doctors diagnose and treat disorders of the small intestine". This report details the development of a robotic enteroscope inspired by snakes designed to navigate the small intestine for enhanced diagnosis and treatment. The system utilizes multifunctional actuators and textured coatings to move through narrow passages by mimicking snake locomotion. It is equipped with instruments for imaging, drug delivery, and taking biopsies of polyps, and external controllers guide the robot through the intestine. Animal studies confirmed the robot's capacity to travel several feet while successfully performing these interventions. This advancement suggests potential applications for minimally invasive medical procedures and further development in soft robotics technology.

items.title: Audi Tests Agile Robots’ Mobile Humanoids for Automotive Parts Sequencing
items.summary: Audi is testing Agile Robots’ mobile humanoids for sequencing automotive parts at its Ingolstadt Production Lab. The project involves picking components from containers and arranging them for assembly, addressing a material-supply operation scale of one million picks daily. The system utilizes dual-arm manipulation and a mobile base to handle varied, unsorted components in logistics environments. Virtual testing using a digital twin supported by NVIDIA Omniverse and Dassault Systèmes is used to assess feasibility before wider deployment. Success in the final deployment will depend on consistent physical performance metrics like pick rates and operating costs.

The system employs dual-arm manipulation and a mobile base to manage varied, unsorted components within logistics environments. items.title: Neura Robotics and TUM open €17 million RoboGym and unveil new humanoid
items.summary: Neura Robotics and the Technical University of Munich opened a €17 million robotics center near Munich Airport. This center features the TUM RoboGym, a facility combining robotics research, training, and industrial applications in over 2,300 square meters. The initiative allows companies across ten industries to train robots in real-world tasks like handling and loading materials. Neura also unveiled its latest humanoid robot, the 4NE1 Gen 4, which is designed for series production and powered by Neuron AI. The partnership aims to advance physical AI capabilities and establish an international network of training facilities.

This facility incorporates the TUM RoboGym, a space exceeding two thousand three hundred square meters designed for robotics research, training, and industrial applications. The center facilitates training for companies across ten industries to teach robots real-world tasks such as material handling and loading. Additionally, Neura Robotics introduced its latest humanoid robot, the 4NE1 Gen 4, which utilizes Neuron AI and is engineered for series production. This collaboration seeks to advance physical artificial intelligence and build an international network of training resources. The developments indicate a push toward practical physical AI implementation across various sectors.

items.title: AGIBOT Introduces Worken, New AI Models and G2 Max at Innovation Day 2026
items.summary: AGIBOT introduced Worken, a framework to measure robot productivity using the formula: Worken = Active Robots × Autonomous Working Hours × Output Efficiency Ratio. The company also unveiled new hardware like AHA3, which integrates locomotion, interaction, and task execution capabilities. Newer AI models include GO-3 Preview for reasoning and action, and WITA-Omni 1.0 for human-robot interaction. The G2 Max robot is designed for industrial handling with a 40 kg dual-arm capacity and a working height range of 0.1–2.5 meters. Finally, Link-U OS 1.0 is an open-source operating system with a roadmap aiming for full open-sourcing by the end of 2026.
items.audio_script: From Humanoids Daily, AGIBOT introduced Worken, new AI models, and the G2 Max at Innovation Day 2026, detailing advancements in robotics and artificial intelligence. The presentation focused on the introduction of Worken, a framework defined by the formula Worken equals Active Robots multiplied by Autonomous Working Hours multiplied by the Output Efficiency Ratio, alongside new hardware and software. AGIBOT unveiled the AHA3 hardware, which integrates locomotion, interaction, and task execution. Furthermore, new AI models were presented, including the GO-3 Preview for reasoning and action, and the WITA-Omni 1.0 for human-robot interaction. The G2 Max robot was introduced, designed for industrial handling with a four-hundred kilogram dual-arm capacity and a working height range of zero point one to two point five meters. Link-U OS 1.0 was also announced as an open-source operating system with a plan for full open-sourcing by the close of 2026. This development signals further integration of measurable productivity metrics and advanced multimodal AI capabilities in robotic systems.

items.title: Interview with Faraday Future chairman: Moving from Chinese robot sourcing to US manufacturing
items.summary: Faraday Future aims to build a US robotics business by establishing a US robot factory by the end of 2026, with the first US-assembled robot scheduled for February 2027. The company seeks to localize production to enhance regulatory compliance, supply chain resilience, and quality control, rather than just moving assembly lines. This transition is supported by leveraging existing EV manufacturing infrastructure to create synergies with robotics development. Faraday Future views vehicles and robotics as complementary parts of a larger physical AI ecosystem, sharing core technologies like AI, perception, and computing. Success is defined by establishing a sustainable US-based physical AI and robotics ecosystem through product launches, manufacturing capacity, and supply chain growth.

items.title: Xpeng Iron batteries enter small batch output ahead of robot
items.summary: Batteries for Xpeng's Iron robot have entered small batch production, though the robot itself is not yet in formal production. Xpeng announced a dedicated solid-state battery design tailored for the robot's limited space, emphasizing safety features like impact resistance. However, the specific battery chemistry remains ambiguous, with reports suggesting a solid liquid hybrid or semi-solid state was used instead of all solid-state. Xpeng plans to achieve mass production of Iron by the end of 2026, with initial commercial roles including in-store assistance.

Reports indicate the battery chemistry remains a point of ambiguity, with some sources suggesting the use of a solid liquid hybrid or semi-solid state rather than an entirely solid-state design. Xpeng has set a target for mass production of the Iron robot by the end of 2026, with initial deployment planned for roles such as in-store assistance. This development indicates ongoing progress in integrating advanced power solutions into autonomous robotics. Industry focus will remain on the timeline for full robot production and battery scalability.

items.title: Robbyant’s Embodied AI Challenge Will Send 15 Teams to a Real-Robot Final in Shanghai
items.summary: Robbyant will send 15 teams to a Shanghai final for its Embodied AI Challenge, a 48-hour hackathon focused on adapting models to physical robots. Competitors will use AgileX Robotics’ Cobot Magic platform for this task. The challenge is based on the LingBot-VLA 2.0 model, with over 1,800 teams registering initially. Final details regarding scoring criteria and robot access are still being finalized. The event aims to assess how effectively vision-language-action models can be adapted to physical hardware.

items.title: Unitree’s Quarterly Revenue Surges 70% as R&D Spending Weighs on Profit
items.summary: Unitree's third-quarter revenue increased by approximately 70% to 665 million yuan. Concurrently, the company's net profit attributable to shareholders decreased by 17.4% to 112.7 million yuan. Research and development spending significantly escalated by 249.6% to 127 million yuan. This increased investment was directed toward embodied-intelligence models and computing capacity. Despite strong sales growth, the profit did not keep pace with the expanding revenue.
items.audio_script: From Humanoids Daily, Unitree’s Quarterly Revenue Surges 70% as R&D Spending Weighs on Profit. This report details the financial performance of Unitree for the third quarter, noting a substantial increase in revenue concurrent with significant investment in research and development. The company recorded third-quarter revenue of 665 million yuan, representing a seventy percent increase, while net profit attributable to shareholders declined by seventeen point four percent to 112.7 million yuan. Research and development spending escalated by two hundred forty-nine point six percent, reaching 127 million yuan, with this increased expenditure directed toward embodied-intelligence models and computing capacity. Despite the strong sales growth, the net profit did not align with the revenue expansion. This trend indicates a period of aggressive technological investment within the robotics sector.

items.title: Warp Sciences emerges from stealth, to apply robotics to drug research
items.summary: Warp Sciences raised $215 million to create chemistry infrastructure using robotics and AI for faster drug discovery. The company is building a U.S.-based contract research organization to combine chemists, robotics, and AI for molecule development and testing. Warp aims to generate real-world data to train AI, enabling labs to test more ideas more efficiently. The company focuses on lead optimization analog synthesis, allowing scientists to quickly compare molecular variations. Warp emphasizes building a sovereign biotechnology partner to ensure speed, quality, and intellectual property protection within the U.S.
items.audio_script: From The Robot Report, "Warp Sciences emerges from stealth, to apply robotics to drug research". This report details the recent fundraising and operational plans of Warp Sciences to leverage robotics and artificial intelligence in drug discovery. The company successfully raised two hundred fifteen million dollars to establish chemistry infrastructure utilizing robotics and AI for accelerating the process of finding new pharmaceuticals. Warp Sciences is developing a United States-based contract research organization designed to integrate chemists, robotics, and artificial intelligence for molecule development and testing. The company intends to generate real-world data to train artificial intelligence, thereby enabling laboratories to test a greater number of hypotheses with increased efficiency through methods like lead optimization analog synthesis for rapid molecular comparison. This development signals a push toward integrating advanced robotics and machine learning into the core of pharmaceutical research.

items.title: Welcome, TORCH HAND 2!
items.summary: TORCH HAND 2 is a robotic hand from TorchKernel Robotics, rated 6 out of 10 on the Humanoid.Guide Hand Score. It excels in dexterity with a 4 out of 5 rating for degrees of freedom but has a lower 2 out of 5 rating for strength. The hand measures 200mm by 105mm by 50mm and weighs 0.48 kilograms, priced at USD 6,500. This balance suggests the hand is more focused on dexterity than gripping power. The product is currently in production, offering a commercially available option for robotic systems.

items.title: Welcome, NE01!
items.summary: NE01 is a 145 cm tall, 40 kg humanoid robot developed by GENISOM AI for research, commercial performance, and tourism. It features an aluminum alloy structure with integrated joint modules, capable of moving at 10 km/h and exerting up to 180 Nm of torque. The robot has verified capabilities in obstacle avoidance and sorting goods, but its navigation and manipulation skills are rated very low (1 out of 5). Despite its design intent for mass production, NE01 is currently considered a preliminary platform with demonstrated, limited functionality.
items.audio_script: From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, NE01!". The robot measures one hundred forty-five centimeters in height and weighs forty kilograms, constructed from an aluminum alloy structure with integrated joint modules. It possesses the mechanical capacity to move at ten kilometers per hour and generate up to one hundred eighty newton meters of torque. Verified capabilities include obstacle avoidance and the sorting of goods, although navigation and manipulation skills have been rated very low, scoring one out of five. Despite design intent for mass production, the NE01 is presently regarded as a preliminary platform with demonstrated, limited functionality. This development indicates ongoing research into the practical application and refinement of humanoid robotics.

items.title: Welcome, CYBORG H02!
items.summary: CYBORG H02 is a robotic hand from Cyborg Robotics, designed with five fingers and a tendon mechanism inspired by the human hand. It weighs 750 grams and has dimensions of 248 × 114 × 52 millimeters. Six electric motors drive the tendon architecture, defining its actuation and joint design. The hand received a Humanoid.Guide Hand Score of 7/10, with a Strength rating of 4/5 and a Degrees of Freedom rating of 3/5. The product is listed as in production with an advertised price of USD 4,000.

items.title: Welcome, Mornine!
items.summary: Mornine is a full-size bipedal humanoid developed by AiMOGA, a Chery Group subsidiary, for commercial environments. It measures 167 cm tall, weighs 70 kg, and features an aluminum alloy structure with electric joint actuators. The robot has a maximum speed of 3.6 km/h and can sort goods and avoid obstacles, with a 3 kg strength capacity. It is currently in production in China and is priced around US$41,400.

items.title: Welcome, W-Bot!
items.summary: A wheeled humanoid robot from Yue Quan Bionics features a compact base and an articulated upper body for manipulation in confined spaces. It stands 178 cm tall, uses folding joints for reach up to 2.2 meters, and possesses 43 degrees of freedom for its arms, each capable of lifting 10 kg. The robot is equipped with onboard computing, depth cameras, LiDAR, and force sensors for environmental awareness and interaction. Its primary functions include sorting goods and assembling products within constrained work areas. The robot is commercially available and is designed for workflows emphasizing reach and compact positioning.
